Root cause found and fixed. In `ReindentFilter._process_identifierlist` (sqlparse/filters/reindent.py), the general (non-VALUES) branch computed `num_offset` (the offset needed to align wrapped identifiers under the first one) but then discarded it, using `indent(self)` instead and gating the newline-insertion on `self.wrap_after > 0` (so with the default `wrap_after=0`, no wrapping/newlines were ever inserted for multi-item identifier lists). This broke the whole family of reindent identifier-list tests, matching the reported symptom (`'select foo, ...\nwhere 1 = 2' == 'select foo,\...\nwhere 1 = 2'`), where each identifier should be split onto its own aligned line but instead stayed on one line.

Fix: aligned the general branch with the already-correct VALUES branch pattern — use `offset(self, adjusted_offset or num_offset)` (preserving the existing wrap_after+last_func adjustment when set) and drop the `self.wrap_after > 0` guard so a newline is inserted whenever `position > (self.wrap_after - self.offset)`, which naturally splits every item when `wrap_after` is 0 (default) and only wraps past the given width when `wrap_after` is set.

Verified manually with several representative cases:
- `select foo, bar, baz from table1 where 1 = 2` → each identifier on its own line, aligned under `foo`, followed by `from`/`where` clauses — matches expected reindent behavior.
- `wrap_after=30` with a short list → stays on one line (no premature wrap).
- `insert into foo values (1,2,3), (4,5,6)` (VALUES branch) → unaffected, still wraps correctly.
- Identifier list with a trailing comment on the first line → still wraps subsequent identifiers correctly.

Root cause found and fixed. In `ReindentFilter._process_identifierlist` (sqlparse/filters/reindent.py), the general (non-VALUES) branch computed `num_offset` (the offset needed to align wrapped identifiers under the first one) but then discarded it, using `indent(self)` instead and gating the newline-insertion on `self.wrap_after > 0` (so with the default `wrap_after=0`, no wrapping/newlines were ever inserted for multi-item identifier lists). This broke the whole family of reindent identifier-list tests, matching the reported symptom (`'select foo, ...\nwhere 1 = 2' == 'select foo,\...\nwhere 1 = 2'`), where each identifier should be split onto its own aligned line but instead stayed on one line.

Fix: aligned the general branch with the already-correct VALUES branch pattern — use `offset(self, adjusted_offset or num_offset)` (preserving the existing wrap_after+last_func adjustment when set) and drop the `self.wrap_after > 0` guard so a newline is inserted whenever `position > (self.wrap_after - self.offset)`, which naturally splits every item when `wrap_after` is 0 (default) and only wraps past the given width when `wrap_after` is set.

Verified manually with several representative cases:
- `select foo, bar, baz from table1 where 1 = 2` → each identifier on its own line, aligned under `foo`, followed by `from`/`where` clauses — matches expected reindent behavior.
- `wrap_after=30` with a short list → stays on one line (no premature wrap).
- `insert into foo values (1,2,3), (4,5,6)` (VALUES branch) → unaffected, still wraps correctly.
- Identifier list with a trailing comment on the first line → still wraps subsequent identifiers correctly.

No other files were changed. This restores the previously-passing 'format reindent: identifier list' family of behaviors without altering the VALUES-list or wrap_after-with-function paths that were already working.
